name: MA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 11 points on the PVI
Auchincloss is a well-funded incumbent with $7.3M on hand
Republican challenger has raised only ~$26K with negligible cash
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly Democratic: an 11-point district lean, a two-term incumbent, and a massive financial advantage over a challenger who has raised almost nothing. Markets and the baseline both put this safely in Democratic hands, so no evidence justifies moving away from a roughly 22-point expected margin.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or a red-wave national environment far worse than current fundamentals assume could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jake Auchincloss seeks another term in a Massachusetts district that voted about 11 points more Democratic than the nation in recent cycles. He enters the general election with a large structural advantage: strong name recognition from prior wins, more than $7 million in cash, and no serious outside spending against him.

Republican Thomas Stalcup faces steep odds. His campaign has raised roughly $26,000 and reported about $1,300 on hand, leaving him little capacity to communicate with voters in the expensive Boston-media market. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent. The expected margin sits around 22 points, consistent with the district's fundamentals and the lopsided resource gap.
